leads.roleSpecificEvidence: EarthDaily Analytics is a Vancouver Earth-observation company developing and commissioning an integrated satellite constellation, ground processing, analysis-ready imagery and geospatial analytics for broad-area change detection. EarthDaily combines a multispectral satellite constellation, cloud-native processing and AI-ready imagery products to support repeatable broad-area change detection and geospatial analysis. EarthDaily reported initial contact with EDC-08 after its July 7, 2026 launch, while EDC-02 through EDC-07 were returning initial imagery and progressing through commissioning; a separate Canadian Space Agency contribution supports an on-orbit thermal-imager demonstration through March 2027.

leads.roleSpecificEvidence: Obruta Space Solutions is an Ottawa space-technology company developing autonomous rendezvous, proximity-operations and docking systems for on-orbit servicing and logistics. Obruta's RPOD Kit combines spacecraft hardware and autonomous flight software for cooperative rendezvous, proximity operations and docking, including navigation-sensor fusion, safe-abort logic and mission optimization. NASA documentation records an autonomous docking experiment on the International Space Station in May 2025 using Obruta flight software, while Canadian Space Agency contributions support POLAR simulation work through July 2026 and modular RPOD-system validation through September 2027.

leads.roleSpecificEvidence: Lux Aerobot is an Alma, Quebec high-altitude-platform company that designs, manufactures and operates stratospheric balloon systems and converts their payload data into near-real-time geospatial intelligence. Lux Aerobot integrates high-altitude balloon platforms, remote-sensing payloads, flight operations and geospatial analytics to collect and deliver persistent regional observations from the stratosphere. A current federal IRAP record supports automatic altitude-control development using coaxial propulsion, efficient motor control and renewable energy, while the company continues to advertise flight-operations roles and active high-altitude platform services.

leads.roleSpecificEvidence: C-COM Satellite Systems is an Ottawa satellite-communications equipment company that designs auto-pointing mobile antennas and related control systems for remote, emergency, government and military connectivity. C-COM's iNetVu portfolio includes driveaway, flyaway, manpack and fixed motorized terminals that automatically acquire satellite links across Ka, Ku, C and X bands. C-COM's July 2026 first-half release reports an installed base above eleven thousand systems in more than one hundred countries, and its current newsroom documents continuing terminal orders and development of transportable LEO-tracking and electronically steered antenna technology.

leads.roleSpecificEvidence: SpaceBridge is a Montreal-area satellite-network equipment company developing VSAT hubs, terminals, modems and managed-network systems for commercial, government, defence and critical-connectivity applications. SpaceBridge combines compact and scalable VSAT hubs, satellite routers, network management and dynamic waveform allocation for GEO and non-geostationary broadband, mobility and tactical networks. SpaceBridge launched its compact UniHUB platform in March 2026 and received a $1.25 million Canada Economic Development contribution running through December 2027 to expand satellite-communications-system capacity for defence markets.

leads.roleSpecificEvidence: QEYnet is an Ontario quantum-communications company developing compact satellite quantum-key-distribution receivers and free-space Earth-to-space key exchange for secure satellite communications. leads.roleSpecificEvidence: StarSpec Technologies is an Ontario space-systems company developing high-precision attitude-determination and control hardware, rapid space-qualification methods, balloon platforms and geospatial software. StarSpec integrates sub-arcsecond star cameras, cogless reaction wheels and onboard attitude-control electronics for high-precision small-satellite pointing and imaging missions. An active $2 million Canadian Space Agency contribution supports the InspireSAT 12U ADCS demonstration through December 2026, and ISED lists a December 2025 StarSpec satellite-spectrum application as under consideration.

leads.roleSpecificEvidence: SBQuantum is a Sherbrooke quantum-sensing company developing nitrogen-vacancy diamond magnetometers and magnetic-mapping software for navigation, geophysical, defence, public-safety and space applications. SBQuantum combines compact nitrogen-vacancy diamond magnetometers with compensation, mapping and interpretation software to measure magnetic fields for navigation and object or subsurface detection. The U.S. National Geospatial-Intelligence Agency documents deployment of an SBQuantum and Spire diamond magnetometer on a MagQuest CubeSat in 2026, while CanadaBuys records a $2.24 million MagAware contract running from April to October 2026.

leads.roleSpecificEvidence: KorrAI is a Halifax geospatial-risk company combining satellite interferometric radar, ground sensors and AI-assisted analysis for wide-area infrastructure, terrain and ground-motion assessment. KorrAI's platform combines satellite InSAR, optical imagery, GNSS observations, site records and risk models to monitor ground deformation and assemble traceable infrastructure-risk assessments. The Canadian Space Agency's smartEarth portfolio lists KorrAI developing a Web-based Open Ground Motion Service for near-real-time permafrost-related infrastructure monitoring, while its current platform continues to combine InSAR, GNSS and multi-source risk evidence.

leads.roleSpecificEvidence: ASL Environmental Sciences is an employee-owned British Columbia science and technology company providing oceanographic instrumentation, Arctic and ice services, and optical and radar Earth-observation analytics. ASL's DeCAF work applies satellite time-series, radar and optical imagery, machine learning and automated change detection to identify landscape disturbances and support wide-area monitoring. A 2025-2027 Canadian Space Agency agreement provides $250,000 for DeCAF-RRT, a wide-area satellite Earth-observation monitoring tool, and the CSA smartEarth portfolio separately describes the toolkit's intended Canadian Arctic and CAF situational-awareness use.
